items.title: Bruce Johnstone interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2013
items.q: I was playing at a jazz festival in Boise, Idaho. Michael Brecker was the headliner.

ctx.x: Are you upbeat or downbeat — no puns intended — about where jazz lives in our culture now?

I’m a little bit down on it I think. I think there’s a lot of ego out there — that jazz musicians are making recordings, and they’re very difficult to sit down and enjoy. They’re so intellectually ahead of the audiences. A lot of audiences go — later for this, and they’re walking away. In fact, I saw this happen. I was playing at a jazz festival in Boise, Idaho. Michael Brecker was the headliner. Michael was brilliant. He had Joey Calderazzo on piano, Reginald Veal on bass, and Jeff Watts on drums. And he was…
I think that’s a really interesting statement. Because it says you are trying to get your message out like a singer. Singers have the benefit and the burden of the words sometimes.
